data.body:
ROOT CAUSE EVIDENCE, found incidentally by the 9a17 agent before I stood down. Passing it over -- I am NOT working this ticket.

THE ACTUAL ERROR from a failing job log (change 2600, base 08a39c39c50d):
  python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/install_review_scanners.py':
  [Errno 2] No such file or directory
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

scripts/install_review_scanners.py arrived in 6125c5345f01. Verified absent on that change's base:
'git cat-file -e HEAD^:scripts/install_review_scanners.py' -> absent.

AND THE GUARD THAT EXISTS FOR THIS CLASS DOES NOT COVER IT: .github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml
is NOT in GUARDED_WORKFLOWS in tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py. That test's whole
purpose is to catch a CI step that cannot run on a tree predating it -- it caught exactly this shape
on change 2600 earlier today for a different step. The new workflow was simply never added to its
list. So the pre-merge detection gap is concrete and small: a hand-maintained list that the new
workflow was not added to.

That is the FIFTH instance today of the same meta-pattern -- a guard that exists but does not cover
the new case because its coverage is hand-registered rather than derived from the tree. The others:
740d (ticket 3476's bare-repo guard, hardcoded 3-file allowlist, missed a file added four days
later), the ADR .numbers collisions (marker created only at authoring time), c379 (ADR 0078 settled
container-vs-type and the scheduler never heard), and 2593 (hard-coded discovery-builder module list
that went stale when a split moved the code). Two of those were fixed by deriving coverage from the
tree instead of listing it; that is likely the durable shape here too.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT -- DO NOT LET THIS EXPLAIN MORE THAN IT DOES. The missing-file error accounts for
change 2600, whose base PREDATES the file. It does NOT obviously account for change 2607, which was
branched from 6125c5345f01 ITSELF, where scripts/install_review_scanners.py IS present, and which
still failed on scanner-integration. Either 2607 fails for a different reason, or something else
about the patchset context is involved. Worth confirming rather than assuming one cause covers both
-- I conflated two questions on this ticket once already.

Still free to read: dispatched run 33839813271 (test.yml against main) answers whether the job is
broken outright or only in the patchset context.
